faq.title: A few things you might be wondering
faq.a1: In SRS (spaced repetition) mode, you check the answer and rate how well you recalled it. That sets the next review date. Difficult cards come back sooner; cards you remember well get longer intervals.
faq.q2: Can I try it for free?
faq.a2: Yes. A free account lets you create cards and review them. Card storage and free AI usage have limits. You can check your current limits in Settings after signing up.
faq.q3: What if I need to study before an exam?
faq.a3: Alongside SRS, there are sequential review, random, sequential, by-date, and cramming modes. Follow your review dates day to day, or use cramming mode for repeated practice before a test.
faq.q4: Do I have to make every card myself?
faq.a4: No. You can get public decks from the marketplace or import CSV and JSON files you already have. Your own decks can be shared by copy, subscription, or snapshot.

science.title: Built on Cognitive Science
science.subtitle: Every feature in Reklue is grounded in decades of peer-reviewed research in memory, learning, and neuroscience.

chart.title: Memory Retention Over Time
chart.subtitle: Traditional cramming vs. spaced repetition
chart.note: Based on Ebbinghaus forgetting curve research and spaced repetition studies. SRS reviews at optimal intervals maintain 78%+ retention even after 90 days.

insight.title: Why does spaced repetition work?
insight.p1: When you recall information at increasing intervals, each successful retrieval strengthens the neural pathway. This process — called memory consolidation — transforms fragile short-term memories into durable long-term knowledge.
insight.p2: The key insight: reviewing too early wastes time, reviewing too late means relearning from scratch. SRS finds the sweet spot — reviewing right before you forget — maximizing retention with minimum effort.

spacing.title: Spacing Effect
spacing.desc: Spreading study sessions over time dramatically improves long-term retention. Our SRS algorithm calculates the optimal moment for each review — right before you forget.

retrieval.title: Active Recall
retrieval.desc: Testing yourself strengthens memory far more than re-reading. Every card flip is a retrieval practice trial that reinforces neural pathways.

consolidation.title: Sleep Consolidation
consolidation.desc: During sleep, your brain replays and consolidates memories. Our day-boundary system ensures reviews align with your natural sleep-wake cycle for maximum retention.

interleaving.title: Interleaving
interleaving.desc: Mixing different topics during study improves discrimination and transfer. Our multi-mode system supports interleaved practice across decks and categories.

difficulty.title: Desirable Difficulties
difficulty.desc: Making retrieval slightly harder paradoxically strengthens memory. The 4-level rating system (Again/Hard/Good/Easy) creates the right challenge level for each card.

adaptive.title: Adaptive Scheduling
adaptive.desc: Each card adapts independently based on your performance. Easy cards space out to months; difficult cards stay close until mastered.
